trust_decision.summary: is_url_safe() and is_redirect_safe() decide whether a URL is safe by parsing a string they first mangled with remove_at_symbol_in_string(), so the host they judge is not the host the caller will dial; the published fix parses the raw URL and rejects any parsed username/password, identically in src/helpers.ts and in the committed dist/helpers.js the package actually loads.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names remove_at_symbol_in_string, and this is its call inside the main validator, immediately before the protocol and hostname checks that follow at lines 512-531.

fix_sites.entry_point: internal helper is_parsed_url_safe(), reached from is_url_safe() and is_redirect_safe()
compiled is_parsed_url_safe(), reached from is_url_safe() and is_redirect_safe()

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: dist/helpers.js:425-461 (is_url_safe) and dist/helpers.js:386-419 (is_redirect_safe), a hand-maintained JavaScript twin of src/helpers.ts that is what the package entry loads (package.json:23 -> dist/utils.js, which requires ./helpers at dist/utils.js:4)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: dist/ is generated tsc output so src/ is the source of truth and a rebuild will regenerate it; and is_url_safe_debug is a FIXME-marked debug/console variant that the code itself says does not match is_url_safe, so it is not a security API.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: URLs that legitimately carry '@' outside the authority, such as https://example.com/@alice or ?email=a@b.com, are accepted today because remove_at_symbol_in_string is applied to the whole URL; an over-broad fix that rejects any URL containing '@' breaks them, and the published fix instead rejects only parsed username/password.

O6_input_shapes: NFKC fullwidth '@' (http://a＠host/) that normalize_unicode turns into '@' before the old stripper removes it
raw tab/CR/LF around '@' that the URL parser strips but the string preprocessor does not
userinfo arriving in a redirect Location hop
bracketed IPv6 literal ([::1]) where the brackets must stay stripped before classification
'@' in path or query, which must still be accepted after the fix (the shape that separates a correct fix from a string-level one)

O7_producer.where: src/helpers.ts:515 — the check hands the URL parser the '@'-mangled string, while the host actually dialled is produced by the URL parser on the raw URL at request time (src/helpers.ts:463)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: is_url_safe_debug(): exported near-copy of is_url_safe that still runs remove_at_symbol_in_string at step 5 and has no userinfo rejection, so a userinfo URL is still judged against a different host
O8_uncovered_routes.where: src/helpers.ts:546 (same logic at dist/helpers.js:463-471); exported at src/utils.ts:20 and dist/utils.js:21
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is explicitly the debug/logging variant, marked FIXME 'do not match is_url_safe' at src/helpers.ts:545, so a solver can argue it is not the security entry point and the advisory only names is_url_safe.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point but a separate hand-written copy; duplicated again in another tree (dist/helpers.js)

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the maintainer already keeps a hand-copied validator variant with a FIXME instead of delegating to is_url_safe, so another copy is in character and would sit outside the published fix

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the barrel already re-exports the whole toolkit including a debug validator, so wrapping validate-then-dial in one helper is the natural next addition and re-creates the check-versus-dial gap
